The **81st Golden Globe Awards** was an awards ceremony for [film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_in_film "2023 in film") and [American television productions of 2023](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_in_American_television "2023 in American television"). It was broadcast live on January 7, 2024, from [the Beverly Hilton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beverly_Hilton "The Beverly Hilton") in [Beverly Hills, California](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Beverly_Hills,_California "Beverly Hills, California"), beginning at 5:00 p.m. [PST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Time_Zone "Pacific Time Zone") / 8:00 p.m. [EST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Time_Zone "Eastern Time Zone"), on [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") and streamed on [Paramount+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount+ "Paramount+") in the United States. It was produced by [Dick Clark Productions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Clark_Productions "Dick Clark Productions"), [Ricky Kirshner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricky_Kirshner "Ricky Kirshner"), and [Glenn Weiss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glenn_Weiss "Glenn Weiss"); the latter also served as director.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Otterson-1)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Donnelly-4)[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Schneider-5)[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Winners-6)[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Winners_List-7)[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-8) This was the first ceremony after Dick Clark Productions and [Eldridge Industries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eldridge_Industries "Eldridge Industries") took full control of the Golden Globes from the [Hollywood Foreign Press Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Foreign_Press_Association "Hollywood Foreign Press Association").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Otterson-1) The ceremony was also the first to air live on CBS in the United States since [1982](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/39th_Golden_Globe_Awards "39th Golden Globe Awards").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Otterson-1) Comedian [Jo Koy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Koy "Jo Koy") hosted the ceremony.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Host-2)

The nominees were announced on December 11, 2023. *[Barbie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbie_(film) "Barbie (film)")* and *[Succession](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Succession_(TV_series) "Succession (TV series)")* both tied for the most nominations with nine each, followed by *[Oppenheimer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Oppenheimer_(film) "Oppenheimer (film)")*'s eight.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Nominees-9)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Barbenheimer-10)[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-11)

The ceremony also featured the debut of two new categories: "[Cinematic and Box Office Achievement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Cinematic_and_Box_Office_Achievement "Golden Globe Award for Cinematic and Box Office Achievement")" and "[Best Performance in Stand-Up Comedy on Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Performance_in_Stand-Up_Comedy_on_Television "Golden Globe Award for Best Performance in Stand-Up Comedy on Television")"[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-New_Categories-12)

Additionally, the cultural phenomenon of "[Barbenheimer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbenheimer "Barbenheimer")" received seventeen nominations, winning seven.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Winners-6)[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Barbenheimer-10)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-15)

## Ceremony information

This was the first Golden Globe Awards ceremony after the [Hollywood Foreign Press Association](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hollywood_Foreign_Press_Association "Hollywood Foreign Press Association") (HFPA) disbanded in 2023. On June 12, 2023, the HFPA announced that all of its rights and properties related to the Golden Globes were acquired by [Dick Clark Productions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Clark_Productions "Dick Clark Productions") and [Eldridge Industries](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eldridge_Industries "Eldridge Industries").[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-16)

On February 21, 2023, the date of the ceremony was announced. It came back on a Sunday night slot after being moved to Tuesday for the previous year.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Donnelly-4) On September 18, 2023, [Glenn Weiss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glenn_Weiss "Glenn Weiss") and [Ricky Kirshner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricky_Kirshner "Ricky Kirshner") were announced as its executive producers and showrunners.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Schneider-5) On November 17, 2023, it was announced that [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") had acquired the broadcast rights to the ceremony, replacing the Golden Globes' long-time U.S. broadcast partner [NBC](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NBC "NBC").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Otterson-1)

The nominations were announced on December 11, 2023, during an event co-hosted by [Cedric the Entertainer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cedric_the_Entertainer "Cedric the Entertainer") and [Wilmer Valderrama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wilmer_Valderrama "Wilmer Valderrama"). Most of the categories were revealed during a live-streaming presentation, while ten of the categories were revealed during another segment on *[CBS Mornings](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS_Mornings "CBS Mornings")*.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Nominees-9)[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-17)[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-18)

On December 21, comedian and actor [Jo Koy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Koy "Jo Koy") was announced as the host.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Host-2)[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-19)[[20]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-20)[[21]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-21)[[22]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-22) Before this announcement, it was reported that a source with knowledge of the conversations told [CNN](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CNN "CNN") that at least five A-list comedic actors, including [Chris Rock](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chris_Rock "Chris Rock") and [Ali Wong](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ali_Wong "Ali Wong"), declined offers to host; the hosts of the podcast *[SmartLess](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/SmartLess "SmartLess")* (actors [Will Arnett](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Will_Arnett "Will Arnett"), [Jason Bateman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jason_Bateman "Jason Bateman"), and [Sean Hayes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Hayes "Sean Hayes")) also reportedly declined the offer.[[23]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-23) That same month, *[TheWrap](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/TheWrap "TheWrap")* reported that 64 voters threatened to withhold their final-round votes in protest, after being told that they would not be given tickets to the ceremony.[[24]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-24)

With the awards no longer being overseen by the HFPA, a new, racially and ethnically diverse group of voters consisting of 300 journalists representing 76 countries selected the 2023 nominees and winners.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-Winners_List-7)

For her portrayal of [Mollie Burkhart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mollie_Kyle "Mollie Kyle") in *[Killers of the Flower Moon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Killers_of_the_Flower_Moon "Killers of the Flower Moon")*, [Lily Gladstone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lily_Gladstone "Lily Gladstone") became the first [Indigenous](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Native_Americans_in_the_United_States "Native Americans in the United States") actor to win a Golden Globe Award, winning for [Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actress_in_a_Motion_Picture_–_Drama "Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama").[[25]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-25)

### Expansion

On September 26, 2023, it was announced that two new categories would be added for the upcoming ceremony: "[Cinematic and Box Office Achievement](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Cinematic_and_Box_Office_Achievement "Golden Globe Award for Cinematic and Box Office Achievement")" (a category for films that grossed at least $100 million domestically and $150 million worldwide) and "[Best Performance in Stand-Up Comedy on Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Performance_in_Stand-Up_Comedy_on_Television "Golden Globe Award for Best Performance in Stand-Up Comedy on Television")" (also known as "Best Stand-Up Comedian on Television").[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-New_Categories-12)[[26]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-26)[[27]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-27)[[28]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-28)[[29]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-29) Some critics felt that the new categories were an attempt to improve the ceremony's viewership and relevance, with comparisons drawn to the [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards")' [attempt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards#Proposed_"Popular_Film"_category "91st Academy Awards") to introduce a [category for "Popular Film"](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Award_for_Outstanding_Achievement_in_Popular_Film "Academy Award for Outstanding Achievement in Popular Film") in [2018](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/91st_Academy_Awards "91st Academy Awards").[[30]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-30)[[31]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-31)[[32]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-32)[[33]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-33)

### Reduction

The two Lifetime Achievement Awards (the [Cecil B. DeMille Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Cecil_B._DeMille_Award "Golden Globe Cecil B. DeMille Award") and the [Carol Burnett Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Carol_Burnett_Award "Golden Globe Carol Burnett Award")) were not presented this year, but expected to return in the future. Executive Vice President Tim Gray explained that with the change in ownership and status, and 25 of the competitive categories expanding from 5 nominees to 6, the increase will also include a reduction with no presentation of the two aforementioned awards for this year. "This is not a permanent change, with future awards slated to be given," Gray wrote in a post on the Globes' official website.[[34]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-34)

### Criticism of Jo Koy's opening monologue

[![](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/be/Jo_Koy_by_Gage_Skidmore.jpg/250px-Jo_Koy_by_Gage_Skidmore.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Jo_Koy_by_Gage_Skidmore.jpg)[Jo Koy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Koy "Jo Koy"), host of the 81st Golden Globe Awards

Host [Jo Koy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Koy "Jo Koy")'s opening [monologue](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Monologue "Monologue") was met with criticism from viewers and critics with many describing his jokes as "cringeworthy", "painful", and "unfunny". Chelsey Sanchez of *[Harper's Bazaar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harper's_Bazaar "Harper's Bazaar")* described the monologue as "awkward" and "distasteful".[[35]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-35) Koy was also criticized for putting blame on his writers during the monologue, coming after the lengthy [2023 Writers Guild of America strike](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2023_Writers_Guild_of_America_strike "2023 Writers Guild of America strike"). Justin Curto of *[Vulture](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vulture_(website) "Vulture (website)")* noted that when some of his jokes fell flat, Koy "immediately threw his writers under the bus... He yelled. 'Yo, shut up. You're kidding me, right. Slow down. I wrote some of these and they're the ones you're laughing at'".[[36]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-36) Marlow Stern of *[Rolling Stone](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rolling_Stone "Rolling Stone")* noted that many of Koy's jokes drew "groans" and "boos" from the audience.[[37]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-37)

Among jokes that drew the most ire were those about the film *[Barbie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barbie_(film) "Barbie (film)")*, and attending nominees [Robert De Niro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_De_Niro "Robert De Niro"), [Meryl Streep](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Meryl_Streep "Meryl Streep") and [Taylor Swift](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Taylor_Swift "Taylor Swift"); the latter's reaction went viral.[[38]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-38)[[39]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-39)[[40]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-40) Shirley Li of *[The Atlantic](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Atlantic "The Atlantic")* wrote: "Practically every joke failed to land, mostly because the punchlines were dated or obvious."[[41]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-41) Nicole Sperling of *[The New York Times](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_New_York_Times "The New York Times")*, who was in the audience that night, wrote that she had "never seen an audience rebel against an emcee so quickly" and cited a prominent film director describing the monologue as a "disaster".[[42]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-42)

Conversely, four-time [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards") host and comedian [Whoopi Goldberg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whoopi_Goldberg "Whoopi Goldberg") defended Koy on *[The View](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_View "The View")*, saying: "These hosting gigs are brutal. They're just brutal. If you don't know the room, if you've not been in these rooms before and you're sort of thrust out there, it's hit or miss. Now, I love Jo Koy, he makes me crazy because he's funny. I don't know whether it was the room, I don't know whether it was the jokes, I didn't get to see it. But I do know, that he is as good as it gets when it comes to stand-ups and it is not an easy gig."[[43]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-43) Actor and comedian [Steve Martin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steve_Martin "Steve Martin") also threw his support behind Koy on [Threads](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Threads_(social_network) "Threads (social network)"), writing: "I tip my hat to anyone who steps out on stage to host a live awards show. It's a very difficult job and not for the squeamish. I know because I'm still throwing up from the last time I did it in 2010. So, Congratulations to Jo Koy, who took on the toughest gig in show business, hit, missed, was light on his feet, and now has twenty minutes of new material for his stand up!"[[44]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-44)

Additionally, comedian [Michael Che](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_Che "Michael Che") supported Koy by writing that "comedians should boycott hosting award shows" on [Instagram](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Instagram "Instagram").[[45]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-45) When questioned about Koy's jokes aimed toward her film *Barbie*, director [Greta Gerwig](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Greta_Gerwig "Greta Gerwig") replied that she was not offended.[[46]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-46) On *[Watch What Happens Live with Andy Cohen](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Watch_What_Happens_Live_with_Andy_Cohen "Watch What Happens Live with Andy Cohen")*, actor and comedian [Kevin Hart](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kevin_Hart "Kevin Hart") said he has "no reaction" to the backlash and went on to praise Koy for being a "phenomenal comedian".[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-47) In a [Facebook](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Facebook "Facebook") post by Filipino actor and comedian [Michael V.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Michael_V. "Michael V."), he posted: "I think Jo Koy's Golden Globes jokes are funny, direct, and pretty much self-explanatory. The last thing Jo Koy should be doing is trying to explain it to people who purposely choose NOT to understand and appreciate them."[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-48)

Koy responded to the criticism in an interview with *[Good Morning America](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Good_Morning_America "Good Morning America")*, admitting: "I'd be lying if [I said] it doesn't hurt," but also admitted, "I had fun. You know, it was a moment that I'll always remember. Hosting is just a tough gig. Yes, I'm a stand-up comic, but that hosting position it's a different style. I kind of went in and did the writer's thing. We had ten days to write this monologue. It was a crash course. I feel bad, but I got to still say I loved what I did."[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-49) In his first stand-up set afterward, Koy mocked the Hollywood celebrities, alluding: "Lot a marshmallows, man. They're delicious, but goddamn, they're soft. I just come from a different time. I see the changes that are happening. I get it, but goddamn, can we fucking laugh at ourselves?"[[50]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/81st_Golden_Globes#cite_note-50)

The **82nd Golden Globe Awards** was an awards ceremony that honored [excellence in film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_in_film "2024 in film") and [American television productions of 2024](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2024_in_American_television "2024 in American television"). The winners were revealed during the live telecast, airing on [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") and streaming on [Paramount+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount+ "Paramount+") on January 5, 2025.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-2) The event was hosted by comedian [Nikki Glaser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikki_Glaser "Nikki Glaser"), making her the first solo female host in Golden Globes history.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-Glaser-3)

The nominations were announced live on December 9, 2024, at a [press conference](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Press_conference "Press conference") at [the Beverly Hilton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Beverly_Hilton "The Beverly Hilton") by actors [Morris Chestnut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Morris_Chestnut "Morris Chestnut") and [Mindy Kaling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mindy_Kaling "Mindy Kaling"), following an introduction from Golden Globes president, Helen Hoenhe.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-Globes-4) *[Emilia Pérez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emilia_Pérez "Emilia Pérez")*, with 10 nominations, became the most nominated comedy/musical film in [Golden Globes history](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Awards#Superlatives "Golden Globe Awards"), just 1 shy of the overall record of 11, set by [Robert Altman](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Robert_Altman "Robert Altman")'s [country music](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Country_music "Country music") [satire](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Satire_(film_and_television) "Satire (film and television)") *[Nashville](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nashville_(film) "Nashville (film)")* in the drama category in [1976](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/33rd_Golden_Globe_Awards "33rd Golden Globe Awards").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-5) *[The Brutalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist "The Brutalist")* received the second-most in film with 7 nominations, followed by *[Conclave](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Conclave_(film) "Conclave (film)")* with 6.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-6) Additionally, *[The Bear](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Bear_(TV_series) "The Bear (TV series)")* led the television nominations with 5, followed by *[Only Murders in the Building](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Only_Murders_in_the_Building "Only Murders in the Building")* and *[Shōgun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shōgun_(2024_TV_series) "Shōgun (2024 TV series)")* with 4 each.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-Variety-7)

## Ceremony information

On August 28, 2024, comedian [Nikki Glaser](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nikki_Glaser "Nikki Glaser") was announced as the host for this year's ceremony, following last year's widely criticized host, comedian [Jo Koy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jo_Koy "Jo Koy").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-Glaser-3) She is the first woman to host the Golden Globes solo.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-8) Glaser herself was nominated for [Best Performance in Stand-Up Comedy on Television](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Performance_in_Stand-Up_Comedy_on_Television "Golden Globe Award for Best Performance in Stand-Up Comedy on Television") for her [HBO](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/HBO "HBO") comedy special, *Nikki Glaser: Someday You'll Die*,[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-Governors-9) but lost to [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix")'s *Ali Wong: Single Lady*.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-10)

The ceremony was held at 5:00 p.m. [PST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_Time_Zone "Pacific Time Zone") / 8:00 p.m. [EST](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eastern_Time_Zone "Eastern Time Zone") on January 5, 2025. It was broadcast live on [CBS](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CBS "CBS") and streamed on [Paramount+](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paramount+ "Paramount+").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-Globes-4) [Glenn Weiss](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Glenn_Weiss "Glenn Weiss") and [Ricky Kirshner](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ricky_Kirshner "Ricky Kirshner") of White Cherry Entertainment returned from last year to executive produce the ceremony, along with [Dick Clark Productions](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dick_Clark_Productions "Dick Clark Productions").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-Globes-4)

On December 3, 2024, it was announced that the two Lifetime Achievement Awards, which were not presented last year, would return this year; however, they were presented during an untelevised gala dinner on January 3, 2025, prior to the telecast, similar to the [Academy Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Academy_Awards "Academy Awards")' [Governors Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Governors_Awards "Governors Awards").[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-Governors-9) The recipient of the [Cecil B. DeMille Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Cecil_B._DeMille_Award "Golden Globe Cecil B. DeMille Award") was [Viola Davis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Viola_Davis "Viola Davis"), while the [Carol Burnett Award](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Carol_Burnett_Award "Golden Globe Carol Burnett Award") was awarded to [Ted Danson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ted_Danson "Ted Danson").[[11]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-11)

*[Emilia Pérez](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emilia_Pérez "Emilia Pérez")* star [Karla Sofía Gascón](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Karla_Sofía_Gascón "Karla Sofía Gascón") was the first [trans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Transgender "Transgender") nominee for a Golden Globe motion picture acting category, for the [Best Actress in a Musical or Comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actress_in_a_Motion_Picture_–_Musical_or_Comedy "Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy") category.[[12]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-12) [Jacques Audiard](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jacques_Audiard "Jacques Audiard"), the director and writer of the film, was one of the most nominated individuals, with a total of three nominations: [Best Director](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Director "Golden Globe Award for Best Director"), [Best Screenplay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Screenplay "Golden Globe Award for Best Screenplay"), and co-lyricist of [Best Original Song](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Original_Song "Golden Globe Award for Best Original Song") nominee "[El Mal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/El_Mal_(song) "El Mal (song)")".[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-Variety-7) The composers and co-lyricists of the song, [Camille](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Camille_(French_singer) "Camille (French singer)") and [Clément Ducol](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Clément_Ducol "Clément Ducol"), tied Audiard for most nominated individuals. Aside from "El Mal", they were also jointly nominated for composing *Emilia Pérez*'s [Best Original Score](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Original_Score "Golden Globe Award for Best Original Score") and an additional Best Original Song nominee: "[Mi camino](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mi_camino "Mi camino")".[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-Variety-7)

This year's nominations were tabulated by [KPMG](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KPMG "KPMG"), the U.S. audit, tax, and advisory firm, taking over [Ernst & Young](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ernst_&_Young "Ernst & Young") after fifty plus years.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-Globes-4)[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-13)[[14]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-14)[[15]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-15) [Netflix](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Netflix "Netflix") received a total of 36 nominations between film and television, the most of any distributor.[[16]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-16)

*Emilia Pérez* is the first non-English-language film (with some parts of English in the film) to win [Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Motion_Picture_–_Musical_or_Comedy "Golden Globe Award for Best Motion Picture – Musical or Comedy"). *[Flow](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Flow_(2024_film) "Flow (2024 film)")* is the first [Latvian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Latvian_language "Latvian language") film to win [Best Animated Feature Film](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Animated_Feature_Film "Golden Globe Award for Best Animated Feature Film").[[17]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-17) [Fernanda Torres](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernanda_Torres "Fernanda Torres") became the first [Brazilian](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Brazilian_Portuguese "Brazilian Portuguese") actress to win a Golden Globe in an acting category,[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-Torres-18) as well as the first Brazilian, first [South American](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/South_America "South America") and first [Portuguese-speaking](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Portuguese_language "Portuguese language") actor to win the [Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Golden_Globe_Award_for_Best_Actress_in_a_Motion_Picture_–_Drama "Golden Globe Award for Best Actress in a Motion Picture – Drama").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-Torres-18) She acknowledged her mother [Fernanda Montenegro](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fernanda_Montenegro "Fernanda Montenegro")'s nomination, for *[Central Station](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Central_Station_(film) "Central Station (film)")* (1998), in the same category at the [56th Golden Globe Awards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/56th_Golden_Globe_Awards "56th Golden Globe Awards").[[18]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-Torres-18)

*Emilia Pérez* and *[Shōgun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shōgun_(2024_TV_series) "Shōgun (2024 TV series)")* were the biggest winners of the night, for film and television, respectively, with four wins each.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-Winners-19) *[The Brutalist](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Brutalist "The Brutalist")* was the next biggest film recipient, with three wins; for television, *[Baby Reindeer](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Baby_Reindeer "Baby Reindeer")* and *[Hacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hacks_(TV_series) "Hacks (TV series)")* each won two.[[19]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/82nd_Golden_Globe_Awards#cite_note-Winners-19)

pergunta: Can you list for me all the brazilian ministers of planning from the beginning of 2018 until the end of 2024
resposta:
Based on the Wikipedia data, here are all the Brazilian Ministers of Planning (under various titles) from the beginning of 2018 through the end of 2024:

---

## Brazilian Ministers of Planning (2018 – 2024)

### 2018–2019 (Michel Temer Government — MDB)

**#28. Dyogo Henrique de Oliveira**
- **In office:** 23 May 2016 – 7 April 2018
- *Note: He served as Minister of Planning during this period, but his tenure began in 2016.*
- Party: Independent (MDB government)
- President: Michel Temer

**#29. Esteves Colnago**
- **In office:** 7 April 2018 – 1 January 2019
- Party: Independent
- President: Michel Temer
- This was the first Minister of Planning under the Bolsonaro government (though the ministry still existed under the Temer administration's structure at that point).

---

### 2019–2022 (Jair Bolsonaro Government)

During Jair Bolsonaro's term (2019–2022), the Ministry of Planning and Budget was **extinct**. The planning and budget functions were merged into the **Ministry of Economy**, headed by **Paulo Guedes**. There was no separate "Minister of Planning" during this period.

- **Paulo Guedes** served as **Minister of Economy** (which encompassed planning and budget functions) from **1 January 2019 to 31 December 2022**.

### 2023–2024 (Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva Government — PT)

Here are all the U.S. Secretaries of Commerce from **January 2018 through December 2024**, including those who served only briefly:

---

## Secretary of Commerce (2018–2024)

### Donald Trump Administration (2017–2021), continued into early 2019

| # | Name | Took Office | Left Office | Notes |
|---|------|-------------|-------------|-------|
| — | **Ellen Herbst** (Senior Official Performing the Duties of the Secretary) | January 20, 2017* | February 28, 2017 | *She technically left before Jan 2018, but she was the acting official during a brief gap when Wilbur Ross hadn't yet sworn in. She served for about 6 weeks at the very tail end of Obama's term and first two weeks of Trump's. Not in the 2018–2024 window strictly speaking, but worth noting as context. |
| **39. Wilbur Ross** | February 28, 2017 | **January 20, 2021** | Served ~3 years and 23 days under President Trump. He stepped down amid controversy over his role in the Mueller investigation and subsequent legal issues. |

---

### Joe Biden Administration (2021–present)

| # | Name | Took Office | Left Office | Notes |
|---|------|-------------|-------------|-------|
| — | **Karen Dunn Kelley** (Acting) | January 20, 2021 | January 20, 2021 | Served only for approximately **two hours** — from noon until ~2 PM, when Wynn Coggins was sworn in as Acting Secretary. |
| **— Wynn Coggins** (Acting) | January 20, 2021 | March 3, 2021 | Served ~75 days as Acting Secretary while Wilbur Ross's confirmation was pending. He resigned in late February/early March after being confirmed... actually he remained Acting until Raimondo was confirmed. |
| **40. Gina Raimondo** | March 3, 2021 | **January 20, 2025** | Served ~3 years and 323 days under President Biden. Resigned to accept an appointment as Vice Chair of Goldman Sachs. This is the longest-serving secretary since Wilbur Ross. |
| — | **Don Graves** (Acting) | January 20, 2025 | January 20, 2025 | *This falls just outside your requested window (after Dec 31, 2024), but I include it for completeness since it's relevant context.* Served only for ~2 hours on the day Trump returned to office. |
| — | **Jeremy Pelter** (Acting) | January 20, 2025 | February 21, 2025 | Served ~2 months as Acting Secretary while Lutnick's confirmation was pending. |

---

## Summary Table (Strictly 2018–2024)

Since no one formally held the position between January 20, 2017 (Ross's departure) and February 28, 2017 (Ross's swearing-in), and Ellen Herbst's acting period ended before 2018 began, the **only full-term Secretary of Commerce during the entire 2018–2024 period was:**

### 🏆 **Wilbur Ross** (February 28, 2017 – January 20, 2021)

He was the sole Secretary of Commerce throughout every year from 2018 through 2024, serving continuously across both the tail end of the Trump administration and the early Biden administration.

---

However, if you want to include **anyone who acted as Secretary during that timeframe** (even though they started or ended slightly outside the strict Jan 2018 – Dec 2024 window), here are the relevant acting officials:

| *(No acting secretaries during 2018–2024)* | — | — |

**Key takeaway:** For the entire calendar years 2018, 2019, 2020, and 2021 (through Jan 19), **Wilbur Ross** was the only Secretary of Commerce. In 2022, 2023, and 2024, **Gina Raimondo** served continuously without interruption. The only "short-acting" individuals during this specific window were acting officials in early 2021 (Kelley and Coggins), each serving far less than a full year.

The **United States secretary of commerce** (**SecCom**) is the head of the [United States Department of Commerce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Commerce "United States Department of Commerce"). The secretary serves as the principal advisor to the [president of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States "President of the United States") on all matters relating to [commerce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Commerce "Commerce"). The secretary reports directly to the president and is a statutory member of the [Cabinet of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabinet_of_the_United_States "Cabinet of the United States"). The secretary is [appointed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prerogative "Prerogative") by the president, with the [advice and consent](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Advice_and_Consent_Clause "Advice and Consent Clause") of the [United States Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate "United States Senate"). The secretary of commerce is responsible for promoting American businesses and industries. The department states its mission as 'to foster, promote, and develop the foreign and domestic commerce of the United States'.[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Commerce#cite_note-2)

Until 1913, there was one [secretary of commerce and labor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Commerce_and_Labor "United States Department of Commerce and Labor"), uniting this department with the [United States Department of Labor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Labor "United States Department of Labor"), which is now headed by a separate [United States secretary of labor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Labor "United States Secretary of Labor").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Commerce#cite_note-3)

The secretary of commerce is a [Level I position in the Executive Schedule](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Executive_Schedule#Level_I "Executive Schedule")[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Commerce#cite_note-4) with an annual salary of [US$](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/US_Dollar "US Dollar") 250,600, as of January 2025.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Commerce#cite_note-Salary-5)

The current secretary of commerce is [Howard Lutnick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Howard_Lutnick "Howard Lutnick").[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Commerce#cite_note-6)

## Line of succession

The line of succession for the secretary of commerce is as follows:[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Commerce#cite_note-13)

1. [Deputy Secretary of Commerce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deputy_Secretary_of_Commerce "Deputy Secretary of Commerce")
2. General Counsel of the Department of Commerce
3. [Under Secretary of Commerce for International Trade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Under_Secretary_of_Commerce_for_International_Trade "Under Secretary of Commerce for International Trade")
4. [Under Secretary of Commerce for Economic Affairs](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Under_Secretary_of_Commerce_for_Economic_Affairs "Under Secretary of Commerce for Economic Affairs")
5. [Under Secretary of Commerce for Standards and Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Under_Secretary_of_Commerce_for_Standards_and_Technology "Under Secretary of Commerce for Standards and Technology")
6. [Under Secretary of Commerce for Oceans and Atmosphere](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Under_Secretary_of_Commerce_for_Oceans_and_Atmosphere "Under Secretary of Commerce for Oceans and Atmosphere") and Administrator of the [National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Oceanic_and_Atmospheric_Administration "National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration")
7. Under Secretary of Commerce for Export Administration
8. Chief Financial Officer of the Department of Commerce and Assistant Secretary of Commerce for Administration
9. Boulder Laboratories Site Manager, [National Institute of Standards and Technology](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Institute_of_Standards_and_Technology "National Institute of Standards and Technology")

# Thiago Laitz

## About

Thiago Laitz developed Exaranker, a neural ranker that uses natural language explanations to rank search results. Laitz is a Research Scientist at Maritaca AI and an Electrical Engineer at Unicamp. They focus on NLP and Information Retrieval, with an emphasis on building Portuguese-language LLMs and efficient ranking systems. Laitz contributed to the Sabiá-3 technical report and created Inranker, a distilled ranking model for zero-shot search. They also developed Bluex, a benchmark for evaluating LLMs on Brazilian university entrance exams, and have studied generative models for synthesizing EEG signals in brain-computer interfaces.

## Papers23

### Sabiá-3 Technical Report

This report presents Sabi\'a-3, our new flagship language model, and
Sabiazinho-3, a more cost-effective sibling. The models were trained on a large
brazilian-centric corpus. Evaluations across diverse professional and academic
benchmarks show a strong performance on Portuguese and Brazil-related tasks.
Sabi\'a-3 shows large improvements in comparison to our previous best of model,
Sabia-2 Medium, especially in reasoning-intensive tasks. Notably, Sabi\'a-3's
average performance matches frontier LLMs, while it is offered at a three to
four times lower cost per token, reinforcing the benefits of domain
specialization.

### BLUEX: A benchmark based on Brazilian Leading Universities Entrance eXams

One common trend in recent studies of language models (LMs) is the use of standardized tests for evaluation. However, despite being the fifth most spoken language worldwide, few such evaluations have been conducted in Portuguese. This is mainly due to the lack of high-quality datasets available to the community for carrying out evaluations in Portuguese. To address this gap, we introduce the Brazilian Leading Universities Entrance eXams (BLUEX), a dataset of entrance exams from the two leading universities in Brazil: UNICAMP and USP. The dataset includes annotated metadata for evaluating the performance of NLP models on a variety of subjects. Furthermore, BLUEX includes a collection of recently administered exams that are unlikely to be included in the training data of many popular LMs as of 2023. The dataset is also annotated to indicate the position of images in each question, providing a valuable resource for advancing the state-of-the-art in multimodal language understanding and reasoning. We describe the creation and characteristics of BLUEX and establish a benchmark through experiments with state-of-the-art LMs, demonstrating its potential for advancing the state-of-the-art in natural language understanding and reasoning in Portuguese. The data and relevant code can be found at this https URL

### ExaRanker: Explanation-Augmented Neural Ranker

Recent work has shown that inducing a large language model (LLM) to generate explanations prior to outputting an answer is an effective strategy to improve performance on a wide range of reasoning tasks. In this work, we show that neural rankers also benefit from explanations. We use LLMs such as GPT-3.5 to augment retrieval datasets with explanations and train a sequence-to-sequence ranking model to output a relevance label and an explanation for a given query-document pair. Our model, dubbed ExaRanker, finetuned on a few thousand examples with synthetic explanations performs on par with models finetuned on 3x more examples without explanations. Furthermore, the ExaRanker model incurs no additional computational cost during ranking and allows explanations to be requested on demand.

### InRanker: Distilled Rankers for Zero-shot Information Retrieval

Despite multi-billion parameter neural rankers being common components of
state-of-the-art information retrieval pipelines, they are rarely used in
production due to the enormous amount of compute required for inference. In
this work, we propose a new method for distilling large rankers into their
smaller versions focusing on out-of-domain effectiveness. We introduce
InRanker, a version of monoT5 distilled from monoT5-3B with increased
effectiveness on out-of-domain scenarios. Our key insight is to use language
models and rerankers to generate as much as possible synthetic "in-domain"
training data, i.e., data that closely resembles the data that will be seen at
retrieval time. The pipeline consists of two distillation phases that do not
require additional user queries or manual annotations: (1) training on existing
supervised soft teacher labels, and (2) training on teacher soft labels for
synthetic queries generated using a large language model. Consequently, models
like monoT5-60M and monoT5-220M improved their effectiveness by using the
teacher's knowledge, despite being 50x and 13x smaller, respectively. Models
and code are available at https://github.com/unicamp-dl/InRanker.

### Sabiá-4 Technical Report

This technical report presents Sabiá-4 and Sabiazinho-4, a new generation of Portuguese language models with a focus on Brazilian Portuguese language. The models were developed through a four-stage training pipeline: continued pre-training on Portuguese and Brazilian legal corpora, long-context extension to 128K tokens, supervised fine-tuning on instruction data spanning chat, code, legal tasks, and function calling, and preference alignment. We evaluate the models on six benchmark categories: conversational capabilities in Brazilian Portuguese, knowledge of Brazilian legislation, long-context understanding, instruction following, standardized exams, and agentic capabilities including tool use and web navigation. Results show that Sabiá-4 and Sabiazinho-4 achieve a favorable cost-performance trade-off compared to other models, positioning them in the upper-left region of the pricing-accuracy chart. The models show improvements over previous generations in legal document drafting, multi-turn dialogue quality, and agentic task completion.

### NeuralSearchX: Serving a Multi-billion-parameter Reranker for Multilingual Metasearch at a Low Cost

The widespread availability of search API's (both free and commercial) brings the promise of increased coverage and quality of search results for metasearch engines, while decreasing the maintenance costs of the crawling and indexing infrastructures. However, merging strategies frequently comprise complex pipelines that require careful tuning, which is often overlooked in the literature. In this work, we describe NeuralSearchX, a metasearch engine based on a multi-purpose large reranking model to merge results and highlight sentences. Due to the homogeneity of our architecture, we could focus our optimization efforts on a single component. We compare our system with Microsoft's Biomedical Search and show that our design choices led to a much cost-effective system with competitive QPS while having close to state-of-the-art results on a wide range of public benchmarks. Human evaluation on two domain-specific tasks shows that our retrieval system outperformed Google API by a large margin in terms of nDCG@10 scores. By describing our architecture and implementation in detail, we hope that the community will build on our design choices. The system is available at this https URL.

### Ticket-Bench: A Kickoff for Multilingual and Regionalized Agent Evaluation

Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed as task-oriented agents, where success depends on their ability to generate accurate function calls under realistic, multilingual conditions. However, existing agent evaluations largely overlook cultural and linguistic diversity, often relying on monolingual or naively translated benchmarks. We introduce Ticket-Bench, a benchmark for multilingual agent evaluation in task-oriented scenarios. Ticket-Bench simulates the domain of soccer ticket purchases across six major languages: Portuguese, English, Spanish, German, Italian, and French. Using localized teams, cities, and user profiles to provide a higher level of realism. We evaluate a wide range of commercial and open-source LLMs, measuring function-calling accuracy and consistency across languages. Results show that reasoning-oriented models (e.g., GPT-5, Qwen3-235B) dominate performance but still exhibit notable cross-lingual disparities. These findings underscore the need for culturally aware, multilingual benchmarks to guide the development of robust LLM agents.

### SurveySum: A Dataset for Summarizing Multiple Scientific Articles into a Survey Section

Leandro Carísio FernandesGustavo Bartz Guedes[![Thiago Soares Laitz](https://proxy.assets.alphaxiv.org/aHR0cHM6Ly9zY2hvbGFyLmdvb2dsZXVzZXJjb250ZW50LmNvbS9jaXRhdGlvbnM_dmlld19vcD12aWV3X3Bob3RvJnVzZXI9SjJkNkxxRUFBQUFKJmNpdHBpZD03)Thiago Soares Laitz](https://www.alphaxiv.org/@thiago-laitz)[![Thales Sales Almeida](https://proxy.assets.alphaxiv.org/aHR0cHM6Ly9zY2hvbGFyLmdvb2dsZXVzZXJjb250ZW50LmNvbS9jaXRhdGlvbnM_dmlld19vcD12aWV3X3Bob3RvJnVzZXI9R0ZaNWl6OEFBQUFKJmNpdHBpZD0y)Thales Sales Almeida](https://www.alphaxiv.org/@thales-sales-almeida)+3

Document summarization is a task to shorten texts into concise and informative summaries. This paper introduces a novel dataset designed for summarizing multiple scientific articles into a section of a survey. Our contributions are: (1) SurveySum, a new dataset addressing the gap in domain-specific summarization tools; (2) two specific pipelines to summarize scientific articles into a section of a survey; and (3) the evaluation of these pipelines using multiple metrics to compare their performance. Our results highlight the importance of high-quality retrieval stages and the impact of different configurations on the quality of generated summaries.

### Measuring Opinion Bias and Sycophancy via LLM-based Persuasion

Large language models increasingly shape the information people consume: they are embedded in search, consulted for professional advice, deployed as agents, and used as a first stop for questions about policy, ethics, health, and politics. When such a model silently holds a position on a contested topic, that position propagates at scale into users' decisions. Eliciting a model's positions is harder than it first appears: contemporary assistants answer direct opinion questions with evasive disclaimers, and the same model may concede the opposite position once the user starts arguing one side. We propose a method, released as the open-source llm-bias-bench, for discovering the opinions an LLM actually holds on contested topics under conditions that resemble real multi-turn interaction. The method pairs two complementary free-form probes. Direct probing asks for the model's opinion across five turns of escalating pressure from a simulated user. Indirect probing never asks for an opinion and engages the model in argumentative debate, letting bias leak through how it concedes, resists, or counter-argues. Three user personas (neutral, agree, disagree) collapse into a nine-way behavioral classification that separates persona-independent positions from persona-dependent sycophancy, and an auditable LLM judge produces verdicts with textual evidence. The first instantiation ships 38 topics in Brazilian Portuguese across values, scientific consensus, philosophy, and economic policy. Applied to 13 assistants, the method surfaces findings of practical interest: argumentative debate triggers sycophancy 2-3x more than direct questioning (median 50% to 79%); models that look opinionated under direct questioning often collapse into mirroring under sustained arguments; and attacker capability matters mainly when an existing opinion must be dislodged, not when the assistant starts neutral.

### BLUEX v2: Benchmarking LLMs on Open-Ended Questions from Brazilian University Entrance Exams

Although Large Language Models (LLMs) excel in many tasks, their assessment in Portuguese has received less attention, particularly for open-ended, discursive tasks that demand deeper reasoning and generation capabilities. While the original BLUEX benchmark addressed the scarcity of Portuguese evaluation datasets through multiple-choice questions from Brazilian university entrance exams, it did not cover the more challenging second-phase examinations, which require free-form written responses. In this work, we introduce BLUEX v2, a benchmark derived from the second-phase entrance exams of Brazil's two leading universities: UNICAMP (Comvest) and USP (Fuvest), spanning exam years 2022--2025. Our dataset comprises 395 questions unfolding into 919 graded subquestions, with 55.7% of questions containing associated images (represented as context-aware captions during inference to enable evaluation across both vision-capable and text-only models). Each question is annotated with subject area, official reference answers, LLM-generated rubric criteria, and six cognitive capability tags. We evaluate 21 state-of-the-art LLMs using an LLM-as-a-judge protocol. Results reveal a 4.92-point performance spread across models (4.18-9.10 on a 0-10 scale), with Mathematical Reasoning and Image Understanding emerging as the hardest capability dimensions. The evaluation code, model outputs, and dataset are publicly available at https://github.com/TropicAI-Research/BLUEXv2 and on Hugging Face at https://huggingface.co/datasets/Tropic-AI/BLUEX-v2.

The **United States secretary of transportation** is the head of the [United States Department of Transportation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Transportation "United States Department of Transportation"). The secretary serves as the principal advisor to the [president of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States "President of the United States") on all matters relating to transportation. The secretary is a statutory member of the [Cabinet of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabinet_of_the_United_States "Cabinet of the United States"), and is fourteenth in the [presidential line of succession](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_presidential_line_of_succession "United States presidential line of succession").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Transportation#cite_note-code-1)

The secretary of transportation oversees the U.S. Department of Transportation, which has over 55,000 employees and [thirteen agencies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Transportation#Agencies "United States Department of Transportation"), including the [Federal Aviation Administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Aviation_Administration "Federal Aviation Administration"), the [Federal Highway Administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Highway_Administration "Federal Highway Administration"), the [Federal Railroad Administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Railroad_Administration "Federal Railroad Administration"), and the [National Highway Traffic Safety Administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Highway_Traffic_Safety_Administration "National Highway Traffic Safety Administration").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Transportation#cite_note-DOTHist-2) As of January 2021, the secretary receives an annual salary of $221,400.[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Transportation#cite_note-Salary-3)[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Transportation#cite_note-4)

[Sean Duffy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sean_Duffy "Sean Duffy") has served as the 20th secretary of transportation since January 28, 2025. He was appointed by President [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump") to serve this position, and was confirmed by the [Senate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Senate "United States Senate") in a 77-22 vote.

## History

The post was created on October 15, 1966, by the Department of Transportation Act, signed into law by President [Lyndon B. Johnson](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lyndon_B._Johnson "Lyndon B. Johnson").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Transportation#cite_note-DOTHist-2) The department's mission is "to develop and coordinate policies that will provide an efficient and economical national transportation system, with due regard for need, the environment, and the national defense."[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Transportation#cite_note-DOTHist-2)

The first secretary of transportation was [Alan S. Boyd](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alan_S._Boyd "Alan S. Boyd"), nominated to the post by Democratic president Lyndon B. Johnson. [Ronald Reagan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ronald_Reagan "Ronald Reagan")'s second secretary of transportation, [Elizabeth Dole](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elizabeth_Dole "Elizabeth Dole"), was the first female holder, and Mary Peters was the second. [Gerald Ford](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gerald_Ford "Gerald Ford")'s nominee [William Thaddeus Coleman Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/William_Thaddeus_Coleman_Jr. "William Thaddeus Coleman Jr.") was the first African American to serve as transportation secretary, and [Federico Peña](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federico_Peña "Federico Peña"), serving under [Bill Clinton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Clinton "Bill Clinton"), was the first Hispanic to hold the position, subsequently becoming the [secretary of energy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secretary_of_Energy "Secretary of Energy"). Japanese-American [Norman Mineta](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Norman_Mineta "Norman Mineta"), who had previously been the [secretary of commerce](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Secretary_of_Commerce "Secretary of Commerce"), is the longest-serving secretary, holding the post for over five and a half years,[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Transportation#cite_note-DOTHist-2) and [Andrew Card](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Andrew_Card "Andrew Card") is the shortest-serving secretary, serving only eleven months. [Pete Buttigieg](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pete_Buttigieg "Pete Buttigieg") is the youngest secretary, taking office at 39 years 15 days old, overtaking [Neil Goldschmidt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Neil_Goldschmidt "Neil Goldschmidt") as the youngest secretary, taking office at 39 years 3 months old,[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Transportation#cite_note-CNBC-5) while Norman Mineta was the oldest, retiring at age 74.[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Transportation#cite_note-DOTBio-6) Buttigieg is also the first openly [gay](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gay "Gay") man to hold the position, as well as being the first openly gay Cabinet secretary, and the first to seek a full senate confirmation.[[7]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Transportation#cite_note-7) In April 2008, [Mary Peters](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary_E._Peters "Mary E. Peters") launched the official blog of the secretary of transportation called *The Fast Lane*.[[8]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Transportation#cite_note-8) On January 23, 2009, the 16th secretary, [Ray LaHood](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ray_LaHood "Ray LaHood"), took office, serving under the administration of Democrat [Barack Obama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama "Barack Obama"); he had previously been a Republican congressman from Illinois for fourteen years.[[9]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Transportation#cite_note-9)

[Anthony Foxx](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Anthony_Foxx "Anthony Foxx") was the 17th U.S. secretary of transportation from 2013 to 2017, when [Barack Obama](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Barack_Obama "Barack Obama") was president. [Elaine Chao](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Elaine_Chao "Elaine Chao"), who served as the [secretary of labor](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Labor "United States Secretary of Labor") under President [George W. Bush](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_W._Bush "George W. Bush"), was nominated by [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump") on November 29, 2016. On January 31, 2017, the Senate confirmed her appointment by a vote of 93–6. On January 7, 2021, Chao announced her resignation following the [January 6 United States Capitol attack](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/January_6_United_States_Capitol_attack "January 6 United States Capitol attack"), effective January 11.[[10]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Transportation#cite_note-10) On January 11, 2021, acting [deputy secretary of transportation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Deputy_Secretary_of_Transportation "United States Deputy Secretary of Transportation") [Steven G. Bradbury](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Steven_G._Bradbury "Steven G. Bradbury") became acting secretary of transportation. Pete Buttigieg served as the 19th secretary of transportation during the presidency of [Joe Biden](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Joe_Biden "Joe Biden").

## Line of succession

The [line of succession](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Line_of_succession "Line of succession") regarding who would act as Secretary of Transportation in the event of a vacancy or incapacitation is as follows:[[13]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Transportation#cite_note-14)

1. [Deputy Secretary of Transportation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deputy_Secretary_of_Transportation "Deputy Secretary of Transportation")
2. [Under Secretary of Transportation for Policy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Under_Secretary_of_Transportation_for_Policy "Under Secretary of Transportation for Policy")
3. General Counsel
4. Assistant Secretary for Budget and Programs
5. Assistant Secretary for Transportation Policy
6. Assistant Secretary for Governmental Affairs
7. Assistant Secretary for Aviation and International Affairs
8. Assistant Secretary for Administration
9. Administrator of the [Federal Highway Administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Highway_Administration "Federal Highway Administration")
10. Administrator of the [Federal Aviation Administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Aviation_Administration "Federal Aviation Administration")
11. Administrator of the [Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Motor_Carrier_Safety_Administration "Federal Motor Carrier Safety Administration")
12. Administrator of the [Federal Railroad Administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Railroad_Administration "Federal Railroad Administration")
13. Administrator of the [Federal Transit Administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Federal_Transit_Administration "Federal Transit Administration")
14. Administrator of the [Maritime Administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Maritime_Administration "United States Maritime Administration")
15. Administrator of the [Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pipeline_and_Hazardous_Materials_Safety_Administration "Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration")
16. Administrator of the [National Highway Traffic Safety Administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Highway_Traffic_Safety_Administration "National Highway Traffic Safety Administration")
17. Administrator of the [Research and Innovative Technology Administration](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Research_and_Innovative_Technology_Administration "Research and Innovative Technology Administration")
18. Administrator of the [Great Lakes St. Lawrence Seaway Development Corporation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Great_Lakes_St._Lawrence_Seaway_Development_Corporation "Great Lakes St. Lawrence Seaway Development Corporation")
19. Regional Administrator, Southern Region, Federal Aviation Administration
20. Director, Resource Center, Lakewood, Colorado, Federal Highway Administration
21. Regional Administrator, Northwest Mountain Region, Federal Aviation Administration

resposta:
Com base na Wikipedia e em outras fontes, aqui está a lista completa dos Secretários de Educação dos EUA no período de **janeiro de 2018 a dezembro de 2024**, incluindo os secretários interinos:

---

## 🇺🇸 Secretários de Educação dos EUA (2018–2024)

### 🔹 Betsy DeVos — Secretária Titular
| Período | Presidente |
|---------|-----------|
| **7 de fevereiro de 2017 – 8 de janeiro de 2021** | Donald Trump |

> ⚠️ Ela tomou posse ainda em 2017, mas esteve à frente do Departamento durante todo o período solicitado (2018–2024). Foi confirmada pelo Senado em 7 de fevereiro de 2017.

---

### 🔹 Interinos durante a gestão DeVos (2018–2024)

Não houve substituições formais durante esse período — DeVos permaneceu no cargo até sua demissão em janeiro de 2021. Porém, vale registrar que **Phil Rosenfelt** havia sido secretário interino antes dela (jan–fev/2017), fora do recorte temporal.

---

### 🔹 Transição para Joe Biden (janeiro de 2021)

Após a demissão de DeVos em 8 de janeiro de 2021, houve dois secretários interinos sob o presidente Joe Biden:

#### 1. Phil Rosenfelt (interino)
- **Período:** 20 de janeiro de 2021 – 3 de março de 2021
- Retomou o cargo interino brevemente após a transição.

#### 2. Miguel Cardona — Secretário Titular
- **Período:** 3 de março de 2021 – 20 de janeiro de 2025
- Presidente: Joe Biden
- Confirmado pelo Senado em março de 2021.
- **Foi demitido por Trump em 20 de janeiro de 2025** (fora do seu recorte final, mas relevante para contexto).

---

## ✅ Resumo do período 2018–2024

| Nome | Cargo | Período | Observação |
|------|-------|---------|------------|
| **Betsy DeVos** | Secretária Titular | fev/2017 – jan/2021 *(inclui todo o período 2018–2024)* | Demitida em jan/2021 |
| **Phil Rosenfelt** | Secretário Interino | jan/2021 – mar/2021 | Apenas ~2 meses (fim de 2021) |
| **Miguel Cardona** | Secretário Titular | mar/2021 – jan/2025 | Demitido em jan/2025 (fora do recorte final) |

---

## 📝 Nota importante

Durante **todo o período de 2018 a dezembro de 2024**, o único Secretário de Educação titular foi **Betsy DeVos**. O único interino nesse intervalo foi **Phil Rosenfelt**, que serviu apenas de **20 a 31 de janeiro de 2021** (após a transição política entre Trump e Biden). Miguel Cardona assumiu formalmente em **3 de março de 2021**, portanto também dentro do período solicitado.

The **United States secretary of education** is the head of the [United States Department of Education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Department_of_Education "United States Department of Education"). The secretary serves as the principal advisor to the president of the United States, and the federal government, on policies, programs, and activities related to all education in the United States. As a member of the [Cabinet of the United States](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabinet_of_the_United_States "Cabinet of the United States"), the secretary is sixteenth in the [line of succession](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_presidential_line_of_succession "United States presidential line of succession") to the [presidency](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States "President of the United States").[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Education#cite_note-2) Prior to its creation as an Executive Department, there was a non-Cabinet level position called the [United States commissioner of education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Commissioner_of_Education "United States Commissioner of Education") who led the [United States Office of Education](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Office_of_Education "United States Office of Education").

The current secretary of education is [Linda McMahon](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Linda_McMahon "Linda McMahon"), serving in this role under President [Donald Trump](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Donald_Trump "Donald Trump").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Education#cite_note-3)

## Function

The United States secretary of education is a member of the [president](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/President_of_the_United_States "President of the United States")'s [Cabinet](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cabinet_of_the_United_States "Cabinet of the United States") and is the sixteenth in the [United States presidential line of succession](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_presidential_line_of_succession "United States presidential line of succession").[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Education#cite_note-4) This secretary deals with federal influence over [education policy](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Education_policy "Education policy"), and heads the United States Department of Education.[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Education#cite_note-5)

The secretary is advised by the [National Advisory Committee on Institutional Quality and Integrity](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/NACIQI "NACIQI"), an advisory committee, on "matters related to accreditation and to the eligibility and certification process for institutions of higher education."[[6]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/United_States_Secretary_of_Education#cite_note-6)
